title: IOC seeks new South Korean broadcast partner as JTBC drops Olympic rights
article_text:
JTBC, the debt-ridden South Korean broadcaster, has terminated its rights agreement with the International Olympic Committee (IOC) covering the Winter and Summer Games through 2032 as part of its rehabilitation plan.

In a statement, JTBC said it hoped the move would “eliminate financial uncertainty and establish a stable management foundation,” adding that it would “continue to communicate closely with the IOC through various channels to address outstanding matters arising from the termination of the agreement,” including remaining broadcast rights fees.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The company said it expects another broadcaster or consortium to secure the rights for the remaining events on the contract, including the upcoming 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, the 2030 Alps Winter Olympics, and the 2032 Brisbane Olympics.

The broadcaster added: “The costs resulting from the termination will be determined through the third quarter accounting process and in accordance with the rehabilitation plan once it is approved.

“By accounting for the expected losses as part of the rehabilitation process, we aim to remove financial uncertainty and sustain growth in operating profit from our core businesses.”

JTBC secured exclusive broadcasting rights covering four Olympic events between 2026 and 2032 after securing a contract with the IOC in June 2019.

The broadcaster had initially planned to resell its Olympic rights to major Korean broadcasters, but negotiations broke down, leaving JTBC to bear the cost of solely broadcasting the games.

JTBC also picked up exclusive rights in the country to soccer’s flagship World Cups between 2026 and 2030 in a deal reportedly worth $250 million. The agreement covers the 2030 edition of the men's soccer tournament and the FIFA Women's World Cup in 2027.

Sublicensing this year’s World Cup also faced difficulties, but KBS eventually agreed to purchase rights to jointly air the tournament.

The financial burden of both rights contracts ultimately led to the company filing for corporate rehabilitation proceedings with the Seoul Bankruptcy Court last June.

In August, a Seoul court approved the broadcaster’s request to begin rehabilitation proceedings, allowing the company to restructure its debts under court supervision.

Earlier this month, JTBC officially started the company’s sale process, with the aim of selecting a preferred bidder in January.

NASCAR Lands Major Sponsorship Deal for 2027 Chase Race
article_text:
Watkins Glen International is getting a new race sponsor to go along with its return to NASCAR's championship stretch.

The New York road course announced Monday that Busch Light will serve as the entitlement sponsor of its 2027 NASCAR Cup Series race, officially naming the event Busch Light at The Glen.

https://twitter.com/WGI/status/2122435803120832560

Scheduled for Sunday, Sept. 19, the race will hold particular significance on next season's calendar. Watkins Glen will be the only road course featured in the 2027 NASCAR Chase, putting a premium on road racing talent as drivers compete for the Cup Series championship.

For Busch Light, the agreement gives one of NASCAR's most recognizable commercial partners an even greater presence during the most consequential portion of the season.

Few beer brands have as deep a history in stock car racing as Busch.

A longtime supporter of the sport, Busch Light currently serves as a Premier Partner and the Official Beer Sponsor of NASCAR. The brand also sponsors the Busch Light Pole Award, giving it a consistent presence throughout the Cup Series season.

Its latest investment puts the brand's name on one of the most anticipated road course races of 2027.

"Busch Light has been part of NASCAR race weekends for decades, and we're proud to deepen that connection as entitlement partner of Busch Light at The Glen," said Krystyn Stowe, head of marketing, Busch Family & Natural Family at Anheuser-Busch.

The financial terms of the sponsorship were not disclosed in the announcement.

After hosting its Cup Series race in May in 2026, Watkins Glen will return to a fall race date next season with considerably more at stake.

As the lone road course on the Chase schedule, the 2.45-mile circuit presents a vastly different challenge for championship contenders accustomed to competing on ovals.

"With The Glen returning to The Chase in 2027, we're proud to build on our road racing tradition together and welcome fans to the Finger Lakes for a fall weekend with championship stakes," Watkins Glen International President Dawn Burlew said.

- Friday, Sept. 17: ARCA Menards Series race

- Saturday, Sept. 18: NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series Mission Foods 200 at The Glen

- Sunday, Sept. 19: NASCAR Cup Series Busch Light at The Glen

Tickets and camping packages for the 2027 race weekend are already on sale through Watkins Glen International.

For the New York circuit, a nationally recognized title sponsor and a race with championship implications make for a particularly attractive combination heading into 2027.

title: The Standard Extends Title Sponsorship of The Standard Portland Classic Through 2030
article_text:
PORTLAND, Ore. — Nov. 18, 2026 — Standard Insurance Company (The Standard) announced today a three-year extension of its title sponsorship of The Standard Portland Classic, continuing the company’s support of the longstanding LPGA Tour event through 2030. The extension builds on The Standard’s initial title sponsorship agreement for 2025 through 2027 and its relationship as a tournament sponsor, which began in 2022.

“We are proud to extend our title sponsorship of The Standard Portland Classic and continue supporting an event that means so much to our hometown,” said Dan McMillan, president and CEO of The Standard. “The tournament brings together world-class competition, a growing audience for women’s sports and a strong tradition of giving back. It also creates meaningful opportunities for our employees, customers and community partners to be part of something special.”

Since its founding in 1972, the Portland Classic has showcased many of the world’s top golfers and raised more than $18 million for charitable organizations. As the longest-running non-major event on the LPGA Tour, the tournament has become an important part of Portland’s sports history and the premier annual professional golf event in the Pacific Northwest.

“The Standard’s continued commitment provides meaningful stability for this tournament and helps ensure that the world’s best women golfers will continue competing in Portland for years to come,” said Mark Ganz, board president, Tournament Golf Foundation. “The Standard is an exceptional partner, sharing our commitment to delivering a world-class event while creating a positive and lasting impact in the community.”

The extension expands The Standard’s relationship with the LPGA at an important time for both organizations. Earlier this year, The LPGA and The Standard announced a partnership naming The Standard as Official Workplace Benefits Partner of the LPGA Tour, giving the company a year-round presence throughout the LPGA season and highlighting The Standard’s experience helping employers and employees achieve financial well-being and peace of mind.

The Standard Portland Classic returns to Columbia Edgewater Country Club in Portland Sept. 13-19, 2027.

title: Lusail International Circuit Announces Doha Oasis as Official Partner
article_text:
Doha, November 18 (QNA) - Lusail International Circuit Welcomes Doha Oasis, Rayyan Water as Official Partners Lusail International Circuit (LIC) has announced Doha Oasis, the multi-experience lifestyle destination, as an Official Partner of the circuit and Event Supporter Partner of three major international race events hosted annually at LIC.

Under the partnership, Doha Oasis will serve as Event Supporter Partner of the Formula 1 Qatar Airways Qatar Grand Prix 2026, scheduled for Nov. 27-29, the MotoGP Qatar Airways Grand Prix of Qatar 2027, scheduled for Mar. 12-14, and the Qatar 1812 KM - FIA World Endurance Championship 2027, scheduled for Mar. 25-27.

The partnership comes as Doha Oasis celebrates its fifth anniversary, bringing together two prominent Qatari destinations that welcome visitors from around the world, reflecting Qatar's growing position as a global destination for sport, tourism and lifestyle.

The partnership gets underway with the Formula 1 Qatar Airways Qatar Grand Prix, taking place at Lusail International Circuit in late November. Throughout the race weekend, Doha Oasis will welcome racing fans in the circuit's Fan Zone, offering engaging interactive experiences.

In 2027, the partnership will continue with the MotoGP Qatar Airways Grand Prix of Qatar from Mar. 12 to 14, followed by the Qatar 1812 KM - FIA World Endurance Championship from Mar. 25 to 27.

Doha Oasis will celebrate the racing season with its campaign, "The Race Has a New Heartbeat", carrying the excitement of Lusail International Circuit into the heart of the city and inviting fans and visitors to extend their experience and enjoy a variety of entertainment and hospitality offerings at Doha Oasis.

In this regard, Lusail International Circuit Management welcomed Doha Oasis as an Official Partner of the circuit, noting that, as Qatar's premier destination for world-class motorsport events, LIC continues to strengthen its partnerships with leading destinations.

For its part, Doha Oasis Management expressed pride in announcing the partnership with Lusail International Circuit as Doha Oasis celebrates its fifth anniversary, noting that the circuit is home to some of the world's most anticipated sporting events.

The management said that the partnership brings together two destinations that welcome visitors from around the world and reflects Doha Oasis's commitment to supporting Qatar's position as a global hub for sport, tourism and premium lifestyle experiences.

Meanwhile, Lusail International Circuit welcomed Rayyan Water as an Official Partner through the end of 2028, reflecting the circuit's commitment to expanding its partnership network and strengthening collaboration with local brands.

In this context, Abdulaziz Ali Al Mohannadi, CEO of Lusail International Circuit, said that the circuit's partners played a pivotal role in enriching the fan experience during race weekends at LIC.

He noted that Rayyan Water had long been an integral part of that experience, expressing delight at welcoming the company as an Official Partner and looking forward to working together over the next three seasons to make every fan's experience at the circuit more comfortable and enjoyable.

For his part, Chairman of Alrayyan Mineral Water Bottling Co. Khalifa Khalid Al Rabban, expressed pride in the company's longstanding partnership with Lusail International Circuit and welcomed its continuation as an Official Partner.

He said that supporting world-class sporting events, including Formula 1, MotoGP and the FIA World Endurance Championship, reflected the company's commitment to providing Rayyan Water to fans and enriching their experience during international events that bring together different cultures and communities.

He added that the partnership also reflected the company's commitment to supporting initiatives that further strengthen Qatar's standing as a global hub for major sporting and international events. (QNA)

title: The billion-dollar boat race: How SailGP is changing the business of sport
article_text:
Andrew Thompson remembers clearly how it all began.

Soon after the 2017 America’s Cup, Sir Russell Coutts, the New Zealand-born sailing legend, and the Oracle technology billionaire Larry Ellison were contemplating how to make the sport more appealing to fans and commercially viable.

They had a broad outline in mind, one that married Coutts’ sailing expertise with Ellison’s brilliant mind, but they couldn’t quite nail down the format.

Coutts turned to Thompson, a former Deloitte accountant with a lifelong passion for sport, who worked on the 2012 London Olympics, widely regarded as one of the most successful ever. At the time, Thompson was chief financial officer of the America’s Cup.

“Andy,” said Coutts. “Me and Larry have got a new idea. Can you put together a two-pager that we can send to Larry next week?”

Thompson, now managing director of SailGP, went to work producing a blueprint which still exists today, based on two core principles: identikit boats because, as Thompson explains, “even the tiniest technological advantage would mean a race is pretty much over before it's begun”, and tight cost controls, beginning with a budget cap of $10 million per season per team.

“We really wanted to put a framework together that meant that all participants had equal terms,” explains Thompson. “That was fundamental to the framework and remains so going forward.

“We designed our central services around us providing the logistics, the maintenance, the engineering to really control costs in that area. Each team has a vote around major changes to that framework. It also allows us to make decisions and drive the potential business forward.”

Thus SailGP was born – a centrally owned, franchise-based sports league that generates revenue through team sales, host-city fees, global sponsorships and media rights.

In five seasons of state-of-the-art, technology-driven, fan-friendly, "wild" onshore racing, SailGP has established itself as one of the fastest-growing spectacles in the world, one that has rewritten the emerging sports playbook, and, with it, gained the epithet of Formula One on water.

Races are held in 13 suitably glamorous locations across five continents, with up to 25 million viewers tuning into the live highlights of any given SailGP event.

In little more than seven years, SailGP has gone from “begging venues”, in Thompson’s words, to holding races, to having destinations clamouring to come on board, and willing to pay substantial host fees for the privilege.

“We've seen a huge spike in demand for host venues, and we currently don't have enough spots to fit them in. As a result, obviously the values of those have increased over time,” he says.

Hosting a race weekend where your city "amphitheatre" provides a stunning backdrop, one that is extremely valuable from a tourism perspective, generates an estimated $20m boost to the local economy. Venues are being locked in for up to five years and ideally longer.

Hong Kong and Rome have recently been announced as venues for 2027. The global footprint has helped to attract premium sponsorship partners like Rolex and Emirates.

“The plan has always been to go to different geographies around the world. The Middle East opened up to us, and we've got some great partners in Dubai and Abu Dhabi.

“We've touched a lot of European countries now. We've now gone to South America, where Brazil was a hugely growing market in terms of viewership. The awareness in the US is growing all the time, as is Australasia.

“I'd say in the next five years, we're looking at more expansion in Asia. I could foresee an event in China. Chinese sailing is booming right now. Japan is very interesting to us, as is Korea. We are very much looking at how we can again broaden the audience. Mexico and India are also very interesting for us.” The eventual target is between 18-20 venues.

The number of boats has risen from four to 13, all but one privately owned, with teams now trading at more than $75 million. A 14th will enter next season.

The most expensive purchase to date was made by Doug Devos, the chairman of Amway, the US-based global direct selling giant, who bought the Danish boat earlier this year for $60m.

For that, the owners get the franchise in perpetuity, which also allows them to negotiate their own sponsorship deals to commercialise the boat; some teams are already breaking even. With the cost base capped, there is potential for considerable upside.

“We're looking for stakeholders that share the same view of the sport as us in that they want it to really be viewed by a new audience,” Thompson says.

“They want to make sailing into a real business, to bring foiling sailing to a new audience and really show that it is a cool sport.”

Team valuations themselves are only going to rise exponentially as SailGP is capping the number of teams at 20, with only one per country.

Boats 15 and 16 will join the tour in 2028. Thereafter, the league will look at how best to expand and over what timescale.

“The demand has been there for us to do that, and we have definitely surpassed our expectations relating to the number of teams.

“There's a wider trend in the sports industry around team ownership being a good investment. We've certainly seen valuations of sports teams in the NFL, Premier League, Formula One going bonkers.

“We've certainly experienced that, and it is a position, hand on heart, I didn't expect us to get to so quickly. If I were to look back now at what we've achieved in these years, it has certainly surpassed all of those metrics that we put together back then,” Thompson explains.

title: EHF’s rights sales model shows early results with deals in 80 territories
article_text:
EHF Marketing’s in-house media distribution strategy is paying early dividends, with the commercial arm of the European Handball Federation growing its existing network of rights agreements globally.

Through existing and new agreements, the EHF Champions League and EHF European League club competitions will be broadcast across 80 territories worldwide in the 2026-27 season.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

EHF Marketing took direct responsibility for the rights management, broadcaster servicing, production, distribution, and content services of its club competitions from the 2026-27 season onwards after the governing body prematurely ended its 10-year contract with sports marketing agency Infront late last year.

The continental body has secured several new media rights agreements across key European markets, the Middle East and North Africa, and the US.

These agreements complement the EHF’s established international broadcast network, including existing partnerships with Viaplay, AMC, Arena Sport and Polsat, among others.

The deals cover a range of distribution channels, including traditional broadcasters, OTT (over-the-top, or streaming) platforms, and club-owned media channels.

EHF Marketing stated that the new agreements “reflect different distribution models and market needs and demonstrate a flexible, market-specific approach to media rights exploitation, taking into consideration broadcaster structures and strategic objectives.”

Key agreements include a recently announced long-term partnership with sports streaming platform Dyn Sports covering Germany, Austria and Switzerland, with matches distributed via its OTT platform. There will also be OTT distribution of matches in Iceland, via Livey.

In France, the competitions will be shown on BeIN Sports, the international pay-TV broadcaster, and Handball TV, the jointly owned OTT platform from the French Handball Federation and the domestic top-flight LNH.

In Spain, TV3 will offer free-to-air (FTA) coverage of Barcelona matches, while all competitions and matches are also available on EHFTV.

Meanwhile, in Portugal, Sporting CP, FC Porto, and Benfica are distributing their matches through club-owned media channels, complementing broadcasts on Sport TV.

In Switzerland, the Swiss Broadcasting Corporation (SRG SSR) will provide FTA coverage of selected matches while MSG Networks will broadcast selected EHF Champions League games in the US.

EHF Marketing claims its direct rights management model has enabled it to gain “greater commercial and strategic flexibility.”

Aurèle Weyeneth, director rights and exploitation at EHF Marketing, said: “Actively managing media rights in-house gives us more flexibility in how we approach each market, both commercially and strategically.

“Our objective is not simply to sign more agreements, but to find the right distribution partners and make our competitions as accessible as possible to handball fans. Whether through traditional broadcasters, OTT platforms or club media channels, each market has its own specificities, and these new agreements reflect our approach.”

Elsewhere, France Télévisions, the domestic public-service broadcaster, has agreed a deal with the French Handball Federation for rights to broadcast the national women's team matches for the EHF Euro 2026 tournament.

From December 11, France Télévisions will broadcast the four main round matches on its channels, along with the semi-final and the final, should France qualify.

Philippe Bana, president of the French Handball Federation, said: “In January, we made the decision to take control of handball media rights to offer our men’s national team the widest possible visibility. We are proud to extend this approach to our women’s national team.

“With BeIN Sports, a long-standing partner of French handball, and France Télévisions, which is reaffirming its commitment to us, the French women’s team will benefit from exposure commensurate with its achievements and the public’s affection.

“Seeing both our French national teams accessible to the general public in the same year sends a strong message for handball, our members, and our partners.”

ESPN gets at least 91 of Major League Volleyball's 140 matches in 2027
article_text:
Major League Volleyball's 2027 media deal spreads a record 140 matches across four partners, and ESPN carries at least 91. Scripps Sports has 15 Friday primetime matches.

This story was produced through MarketScale. See how Sports & Entertainment teams put it to work with Events & Onsite Capture.

Thursday nights go to Peacock. Friday nights go to Scripps Sports and ION. Weekends go to ESPN. That's how Major League Volleyball's 2027 media lineup, announced November 17, lays out a league-record 140 matches across four partners. Sports Video Group reported that NBC Sports and ESPN are new to the league, and Scripps Sports/ION and CBS Sports are coming back.

The 140 is the headline number, but where those matches land matters more. For a brand weighing a women's volleyball buy, or a league executive studying how a fourth-year property built a national footprint, the split across partners is what to read first.

In its own release, the league says it designed the schedule around a steady weekly rhythm, with set nights of volleyball on each platform. The league's viewing guide spells out what a fan needs for each window, and that's the detail an ad buyer should care about:

- NBC Sports: each Thursday for 16 weeks, Peacock streams a weekly MLV Match of the Week, available with Peacock Premium or a higher tier. On April 11, 2027, one match moves to the NBC broadcast network: the new Minnesota Forge host the defending champion Dallas Pulse.

- Scripps Sports and ION: 18 matches, 15 of them in Friday primetime. They start on the free Scripps Sports Network and move to ION after All-Star weekend. ION is again the exclusive home of Championship Weekend, both semifinals and the final.

- ESPN: at least 91 matches on weekends and other weeknights across ESPN networks. Matches also stream on Disney+ in select international countries, and the MLV Draft airs November 23 at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN+.

- CBS Sports: the All-Star Match on March 27 on CBS, also streaming on Paramount+, plus 10 matches on CBS Sports Network.

Set nights are something a media planner can actually plan around. Sixteen straight Thursdays on one platform works like a recurring placement, a time slot a sponsor can build a season of creative for. It's a different buy from a handful of big one-off events. ESPN's release, from its press room, describes the deal as putting MLV next to the network's wider women's sports programming. Partners also get distinct roles: Peacock gets a weekly franchise and Scripps owns Friday.

CBS is the continuity in the lineup. In the league's release, Billy Stone of CBS Sports noted that his network has worked with Major League Volleyball from the league's very start. Jon Miller of NBC Sports described the network's arrival as a way to put more of volleyball's biggest moments in front of fans nationwide, which fits a package built around one broadcast-network date and a weekly streaming slot.

The cost of entry also changes by night. According to the viewing guide, Scripps Sports Network costs nothing on FAST platforms such as Tubi, Samsung TV Plus, Amazon Prime, Fire TV and Google TV. ESPN's matches sit in the ESPN App, which viewers reach with a subscription or through certain pay TV packages, and a Disney+, Hulu and ESPN bundle is also available. Compared with Peacock's Premium requirement, that makes Friday the league's free entry point and turns the rest of the week into a series of subscription decisions.

ESPN networks carry at least 91 of the 140 matches, mostly on weekends and other weeknights. The over-the-air windows sit elsewhere: Scripps Sports carries 18 matches, including 15 on Friday nights in primetime, plus the April 11 NBC match and the All-Star Match on CBS. Peacock has a Thursday Match of the Week for 16 weeks, and CBS Sports Network carries 10 matches.

ION gives the package wide reach. The league's viewing guide says ION reaches more than 128 million homes, delivered over the air and via cable, satellite and streaming platforms.

This is our read, not something the league has said: for a sponsor whose brief is awareness, the Friday block and the two broadcast-network dates are where most new viewers are likely to find the sport. For a sponsor that wants to reach the same engaged fan over and over, ESPN's volume and Peacock's weekly run make more sense. The strongest objection is that the split looks sharper on paper than in a real living room. A household with a pay TV package can get most of it, and the announcement doesn't say how ESPN's 91 matches divide between linear channels and ESPN+.

Sports Business Journal's account adds a wrinkle: it puts the at-least-91 matches on ESPN+ via the ESPN App, where the league and ESPN releases say "ESPN networks." For a buyer, that wording is the difference between a streaming audience and a linear one, so it's the first line item worth checking against the full schedule.

Scripps already had a history with the league. Maria Kholodova reported in SportBusiness on March 24, 2026, that a 12-game MLV package was part of the lineup when Scripps Sports Network launched as a free ad-supported television (FAST) channel. Under the 2027 deal, coverage shifts to ION once All-Star weekend is over. In the league's release, Scripps Sports president Brian Lawlor said the company took pride in the part its MLV partnership this past season played in the rising worldwide popularity of volleyball.

title: Tour de France widens sponsorship gap over Giro and Vuelta, says GlobalData
article_text:
The Tour de France has cemented its commercial dominance over cycling’s other two Grand Tours in 2026, leading on sponsorship value, media reach and prize money, according to GlobalData.

The firm’s report, “Post-Event Analysis – Cycling Grand Tours 2026”, found that the Giro d’Italia signed the highest number of partners and the Vuelta a España leaned on its shared organiser ASO, but neither matched the Tour’s long-term commercial power.

Value at the Tour is concentrated among a small group of jersey and main partners. LCL, E.Leclerc, Skoda, Krys, Continental and Groupama together account for more than half of the race’s sponsorship value.

Olivia Snooks, sport analyst at GlobalData, said: “The Tour de France remains cycling’s most valuable property by some distance. Its jersey sponsors are mostly French brands buying national visibility, and media contracts running to 2030 give ASO a secure revenue base. Even with live UK coverage moving behind a paywall for the first time in four decades, TNT Sports reported strong audience growth, which shows how much demand the race commands.”

The Tour also has the broadest media footprint of the three races. Free-to-air television remains the backbone of both the Tour and the Vuelta, reflecting ASO’s preference for public service broadcasters that maximise reach for sponsors. As ASO organises the Tour and co-organises the Vuelta, the two races share most of their broadcasters, with most media deals secured to the end of the decade.

The Giro, organised by RCS Sport, sells its rights separately and relies more on pay-TV. It has confirmed long-term terms for only one of its media deals, with Warner Bros. Discovery.

Snooks said: “The Giro sells volume and destinations. It has the largest sponsor roster of the three races, but regional governments and tourism bodies, from Friuli Venezia Giulia to Abruzzo and Valle d’Aosta, fund almost a third of its sponsorship value as they pay to host stages and promote themselves.

“The Bulgarian Grande Partenza delivered record audiences for Eurosport and HBO Max, but since Enel’s long-running deal ended, the maglia rosa has relied on stopgap sponsors. Securing a long-term anchor partner remains the Giro’s main commercial gap.”

The Vuelta has the smallest sponsorship portfolio of the three and no dominant partner. Title sponsor Carrefour leads a roster built mostly on modest deals with Spanish brands.

Prize money follows the same hierarchy: Tadej Pogačar’s winner’s prize at the Tour was nearly double what Jonas Vingegaard earned for winning the Giro, and more than three times Enric Mas’ prize for winning the Vuelta.

Snooks added: “Pogačar and Vingegaard shaped the 2026 season. One won the Giro, the other the Tour, and both crashed out of another Grand Tour. The drop in online engagement at the Vuelta after Pogačar’s exit shows both the value and the risk of relying on a few headline names. For the Vuelta, larger stand-alone Spanish and international partnerships would help narrow the gap with its two bigger rivals, rather than relying on agreements shared with the Tour.”

title: Snapdragon Bets On F1's Youngest-Ever Champion To Sharpen Sports Marketing Returns For Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM)
article_text:
When Kimi Antonelli claimed the Formula 1 World Championship title this month at just 20 years old, chipmaker Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM) already had him under contract.

Qualcomm’s consumer-facing brand Snapdragon had signed Antonelli as a brand ambassador, a move now anchored by a new anthem film timed to the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix on November 21.

The campaign marks a deliberate shift in how Qualcomm approaches sports sponsorship, prioritizing measurable returns over the prestige-driven partnerships the company pursued in previous years.

Snapdragon’s current deal with the Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula 1 team, of which Antonelli is a driver, launched in 2023 and was built from the outset around marketing accountability.

That contrasts sharply with Qualcomm’s earlier Mercedes partnership from the 2010s, which CMO Don McGuire acknowledged was not “ROI-driven, marketing-driven” in its orientation.

McGuire, who took the CMO role in 2021, is now overseeing a strategy that extends the brand relationship from content and storytelling into activations and hospitality.

“We believe we’re already seeing higher ROI coming out of some things that we’ve done in the short term,” McGuire said, signaling confidence in the retooled approach.

One structural challenge facing the campaign is Apple TV’s exclusive U.S. broadcast rights to F1, which blocks brands like Snapdragon from placing traditional television ads around domestic race coverage.

Rather than treating that as a ceiling, the brand is routing the anthem film through Sky broadcasts outside the United States, alongside digital placements and partnerships with Sports Illustrated and YouTube.

“We’ve got other ways to bring it to life,” McGuire said of the campaign’s distribution strategy around the Las Vegas race.

Antonelli’s historic championship adds significant organic reach to the partnership, as the Italian driver’s record-breaking season has drawn sustained global media attention throughout the year.

Snapdragon’s sports marketing ambitions extend well beyond the paddock, with the brand also holding a sponsorship deal with what McGuire describes as the world’s biggest soccer property.

That soccer partnership has generated what McGuire called “humongous ROI,” and it now serves as the internal benchmark against which all other sports deals are measured.

“When you’re dealing with a sports brand that big, at scale, the brand can withstand the ebbs and flows of performance on the pitch because the fan base is so huge,” McGuire explained.

He added: “That’s the benchmark that we use [for sports partnerships] and maybe it’s a little unfair because they are arguably the biggest sports brand in the world.”

The Antonelli signing reflects a broader industry trend of brands pursuing younger, generationally resonant athletes as Formula 1 continues expanding its commercial footprint in North America.

title: Lando Norris, Max Verstappen confident in F1's decision to race in Middle East
article_text:
Lando Norris is confident Formula 1 bosses are not putting the sport's 2,000-strong travelling circus at risk by ending the season in the Middle East.

Following Saturday's race on the Las Vegas Strip, the grid's 11 teams -- 10 of which have bases in the UK -- will head to Qatar for the penultimate round on Nov. 29 before a concluding fixture in Abu Dhabi the following weekend.

Imola had been placed on standby to host the final race amid the ongoing United States-Iran conflict.

However, F1 chiefs confirmed last week that they will push ahead with completing the 23-round season, as planned, in the Middle East.

UK's current Foreign Office advice says the situation in the region "remains deeply unpredictable and the risk of escalation is high."

It adds that "British nationals in, or planning to travel through, the Middle East should be prepared for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions," as well as "a risk of further attacks across the region at short notice."

But speaking in Las Vegas, 27-year-old Norris, who won the previous race in São Paulo, said: "I am looking forward to going. From my side, I am fine. It is a big team that we travel with, and it is more, 'what do they think?'

"But I have my friend's wedding in Bahrain next week, so I was planning on going there anyway, and then going on to Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

"So, from my side, it is not a concern. I just don't believe that this sport would put us at risk."

The rounds in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were cancelled earlier this year, although a 'Bahrain Grand Prix' was relocated to Malaysia's Sepang venue last month. Next year's calendar is due to begin in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

"I don't have any hesitation to go or know of anyone that is concerned," said Mercedes driver George Russell ahead of the concluding two rounds.

"I am sure some people have their reservations. But I know people who live in the region, and they have said it quite bluntly, that if they didn't feel comfortable, they wouldn't remain there with their families.

"There are a lot of terrible things going on in every region of the world, and you have got to trust in the people that say it is safe. F1 are not stupid, so there is zero concern from my side. Fingers crossed it'll all be fine."

Max Verstappen, who previously said in September that he would prefer F1 not to race in the Middle East, said otherwise in Vegas.

Verstappen, quoted by BBC Sport, said: "I trust F1 and FIA to make the right call on that, right?

"I don't have all the intel. I'm not an officer. I just hope that they make the right call on that. And that's all that you can rely on, really.

"They also send over their findings and understanding. So I trust them."

Kimi Antonelli was crowned world champion last month in Mexico, while his Mercedes team wrapped up the constructors' title the following weekend in São Paulo.

Red Bull's Verstappen leads the battle to finish as runner-up in the drivers' standings. The four-time world champion is 17 points clear of Russell and 18 ahead of Lewis Hamilton ahead of Saturday's night race.

title: F1 drivers welcome prospect of V8 return after FIA president's signal
‘It felt like the time was right for something new’ – Piastri opens up on decision to split with management team
article_text:
Oscar Piastri has reflected on the decision to part ways with his management team, led by nine-time Grand Prix winner Mark Webber and his partner Ann Webber.

Oscar Piastri has explained why he and his management team, led by Mark and Ann Webber, mutually agreed to part ways, with the Australian believing the time was right for a new chapter in his career.

The decision was announced following the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, bringing an end to a partnership that began in 2019 and helped Piastri secure his Formula 1 debut with McLaren in 2023.

Speaking to the media in Las Vegas, Piastri reflected on the contribution the Webbers had made to his career, explaining that both parties had reached a point where pursuing separate paths felt like the right decision.

"We were just getting to a stage in our collaboration where it was better for us to go on our separate paths," he said.

"Mark and Ann contributed so much to my career, both in placing me where I am today and the management of everything behind the scenes that nobody ever really sees. It felt like the time was right for something new."

The Webbers had already reduced their trackside involvement during the 2026 season, with Piastri's former PREMA race engineer Pedro Matos and mental coach Emma Murray taking on greater roles within his close team.

Asked whether a different management structure could benefit his performances, Piastri reiterated his appreciation for the support he had received throughout his junior career and first four seasons in F1.

"Mark played a massive part in my career, both Mark and Ann, at the end of my junior career, setting me up in Formula 1 and guiding me through those first few years," he added. "The impact they've had on my career has been enormous, and I think now it feels like the right time for us both to go on our separate adventures.

"I think having the structure around you is an important thing, and it has looked a bit different this year already and will look a bit different again in the future, probably. But they played a big part in where my career is today, so I'm very, very grateful for everything they did."

While Piastri looks ahead to a new chapter off the track, his immediate focus remains on maximising his results in the final three rounds of the 2026 season, beginning with a challenging weekend in Las Vegas.

"Vegas is always unique as a weekend, and as an event," the Australian driver explained when asked about how he plans to approach the race.

"We're going to be starting a little further behind, no matter where we qualify, so it's just trying to maximise what we can. We don't know exactly where we're going to sit with things. Hopefully, the new engine is going to help out a little bit, but there's obviously going to be some spots to make up."

Despite some frustrating results in recent rounds, Piastri believes his feeling with the MCL40 has improved, particularly in Malaysia, Singapore, Baku and Brazil. The Australian pointed to his race pace at Interlagos as an encouraging sign, even if his qualifying performance prevented him from fully capitalising on that potential.

"I felt like through Malaysia, Singapore and Baku, and then Brazil as well, the results weren't always what they could have been, but the feeling in the car was definitely an improvement," he explained. "In Brazil, Qualifying was a shame because the pace I had on Sunday was the strongest that it's been for a while.

"That's the big positive. It's just about trying to convert that potential now into results."

title: Blast and Fever partner in live events ticketing deal
article_text:
Ticketing and entertainment tech provider Fever has entered into a deal with heavyweight esports organization Blast, running through 2029.

Through a tie-up unveiled today, Fever becomes the esports organization's exclusive ticketing partner across its entire live events portfolio.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Fever will work to integrate ticket searches, purchasing, transfers, and event access into one platform.

Fever's technology will be integrated into the various Blast online platforms, while tickets will also be sold through Fever's sales channels.

In addition, Fever will provide Blast with on-site ticketing operations, including "secure access-control technology and box-office terminals, alongside 24/7 multilingual customer support."

Marketing and promotion will also be provided by Fever through the deal.

Overall, this forms part of the wider Blast efforts to ramp up the live events side of its business.

James Woollard, Blast's vice president of destinations and marketing, commented: "Partnering with Fever allows us to bring more of that journey together in one place, making it easier for fans to discover our events, buy with confidence, securely resell or transfer tickets and personalise their experience after purchase.”

This month has already seen Fever unveil a deal with the Premier Jumping League (PJL), the new global show jumping competition launching next year.

In mid-October, meanwhile, Fever was announced as the ticketing platform partner for the X Games action sports property.

title: Scottish Rugby extends two partnership agreements
article_text:
Saltire Energy has agreed a three-year extension to a relationship that began in 2021. The Aberdeen-based company will continue to support Scotland Men’s international matchdays alongside two grassroots programmes, the Saltire Energy Rugby Schools Week and Saltire Energy Caledonia Cup.

The Schools Week programme has engaged more than 70,000 pupils at over 600 state schools since its launch in 2021 and forms part of Scottish Rugby’s State School Strategy. The Saltire Energy Caledonia Cup also brought together more than 600 young players for its regional Finals Day in March.

Alongside that agreement, Highland Spring has extended its exclusive relationship with Scottish Rugby for a further two years and will remain Official Water Supplier until at least 2028.

Since the partnership began in 2024, Highland Spring has supplied more than 90,000 litres of water to Scotland’s men’s, women’s and U20 teams, as well as Glasgow Warriors and Edinburgh Rugby.

The next phase of the partnership will include increased on-field visibility, further content around hydration and a coaching session or community day at a local rugby club involving a former Scotland player. Highland Spring products will also remain available at Scottish Gas Murrayfield, alongside a recycling programme for empty bottles.

The partnership generated 5.4 million social and digital impressions across its first two seasons, according to Scottish Rugby, while television exposure reached 9.56 million during 2025/26.

Together, the two renewals extend support across both elite and grassroots rugby in Scotland. While Saltire Energy will continue its involvement with international matchdays and youth participation, Highland Spring will retain a role spanning Scotland’s national teams, professional clubs, supporters and community activity

Simon Oldham, Managing Director of Highland SpringGroup, said, “Highland Spring and Scottish Rugby are two Scottish icons, perfectly matched through shared values and a passion for helping people perform at their best. Over the past two years, we’ve built an authentic and highly collaborative relationship – and this extension marks a bold next chapter

“Healthy hydration is essential to performance on and off the pitch. Our increased investment will help us take that message to even more people while continuing to hydrate Scotland’s players and supporters.”

Olaf Gueldner, Chief Customer Officer at Scottish Rugby, said, “The commitment from Saltire Energy to Scottish Rugby over the duration of the partnership is testament to the many shared values between our organisations. We are both passionate about supporting the game at grassroots level through our community clubs and schools.

Mike Loggie, CEO of Saltire Energy, said, “Saltire Energy is proud to continue our official partnership with Scottish Rugby. As we celebrate our 40th year in business, our partnership with SRU reinforces our commitment to the communities we operate in and our dedication to the role sport plays in young people’s lives.”

title: Future imperfect: What's behind the abortive 2030 F1 rules announcement?
article_text:
Future imperfect: What's behind the abortive 2030 F1 rules announcement?

Famously, when the papal conclave gathers to elect a new pope, a successful vote is communicated to the huddled masses via smoke from the Sistine Chapel chimney as the chemically impregnated ballot papers are burned: white smoke signifies a decision, black means yet another round of voting. The practice derives from the 13th century, when the cardinals took three years to debate a successor to Clement IV, prompting the frustrated local faithful to lock them inside the palace with only bread and water to subsist upon.

All this came to mind when Monday's much-anticipated meeting between the engine manufacturers, the FIA and the commercial rights holder to discuss the next generation of Formula 1 engines was followed by the 21st century F1 equivalent of white smoke billowing from the chimney: an Instagram post by FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem.

“You spoke, we listened. V8s coming soon,” he wrote underneath the ‘asset', an FIA-branded graphic illustrating sound waves and accompanied by the unmistakeable scream of a high-revving V8 engine.

And then, almost within the blinking of an eye, the white smoke turned black. Various related promulgations on the FIA's other social media channels were deleted, kept for posterity only by those with the foresight to screenshot them.

Ben Sulayem has been among the most vocal exponents not only of a return to ‘purer' racing engines than the current turbocharged hybrid V6s, but also of an earlier timing for that change. Although the balance of electrical deployment to internal combustion engine power is shifting over the next couple of seasons, the essential concept is due to remain in place until 2031.

Speaking earlier this season, the FIA president made it clear he wants to bring forward a new generation of engines in 2030, and would use all the powers at his disposal to make it so. But while it is within Ben Sulayem's bailiwick to set the F1 technical rules, whether the other stakeholders in grand prix racing would sign up to that is another matter, and bound into the commercial settlement known as the Concorde Agreement.

Realistically, Ben Sulayem requires a consensus between the FIA, the teams, the manufacturers and the commercial rights holder. Aligning these parties – some of whom are in competition with one another – is usually a process that is both tormented and tormenting.

It's in that context we must view this week's announcements and their subsequent striking from the record.

What is understood from various briefings is that there was broad agreement for a turbocharged 2.1-litre V8 with a smaller electrical element. Even to get to this point has required a great deal of compromise, since Ben Sulayem's spoken preference was for naturally aspirated V8s with token electrical input, similar to the Kinetic Energy Recovery System (KERS) first seen in 2009.

The president sees simplification as the way of creating a virtuous circle: manufacturing and development would cost less, potentially opening the way for non-manufacturer engines, while the engines themselves would be lighter. This would make a lower minimum weight for the cars realistically achievable.

This met with considerable resistance from the car manufacturers – although, to complicate the debate further, these are not all aligned with one another. Ford and Cadillac, for instance, with their broader focus on the US market, are understood to have been supportive of dropping turbos and having a smaller but still significant electrical element. At the other end of the scale, Audi and Honda saw natural aspiration as a deal-breaker and were insistent on a strong element of hybridisation.

Adding two cylinders was much less of an issue since V8 engines still figure largely in several key road car markets. In racing terms, V6s make a much less inspiring noise owing to their ugly firing order, even when not breathing via a forced induction system which mutes the soundtrack.

Although the principle of turbocharging will most likely remain, it will be based on smaller compressors running with lower boost pressures, which will reduce lag. The electrical motor's output will be reduced from the current maximum of 350 kilowatts (kW) to 100kW in general running, with another 100kW available to augment overtaking.

While this was the understanding, it's clear now that several of the parties in Monday's meeting emerged with a different perception to the governing body about what had actually been agreed.

This isn't necessarily a setback to the process, even though it has exposed a certain lack of consensus as we approach the point where the rules must be set. One thing all the manufacturers appear to agree on is that they need clarity by the end of this year to have enough development runway for a 2030 introduction.

To that end, the FIA wants to present a definitive 2030 regulatory framework to the World Motor Sport Council meeting in Shanghai on 10 December. This, though, would essentially be a rubber-stamping process. The real agreement must be secured before then.

This week's premature celebration suggests that this agreement is close enough to have the press releases written, but not yet at the point of clicking ‘send'. Perhaps we should lock the stakeholders in a nearby palace and feed them only bread and water until unanimity breaks out?

title: "We haven't taken any steps backwards" – McLaren boss explains 2026
article_text:
McLaren's 2026 Formula 1 season has been characterised by a recovery effort that never quite came to fruition.

Yet, team principal Andrea Stella insists the reasons for this are well understood, so he can be optimistic about 2027: "We are in a completely different place compared to the start of the season," he told Motorsport.com.

Whenever it seemed to have caught its rivals, McLaren found itself falling behind once again. A difficult start, followed by progress that culminated in a period of the championship when the MCL40 appeared capable of setting the technical benchmark, then a gradual decline in competitiveness and a return to the front at the Brazilian Grand Prix. This trajectory is not easy to interpret.

Stella has an explanation that goes beyond the performance of individual upgrades. He traces the team's 2026 difficulties back to what happened during the previous season, identifying three decisive factors: a delay in developing the new car, the consequences of the demands placed on the team by the 2025 championship battle, and the disadvantages of being a Mercedes customer team at the beginning of the new regulatory era.

"I don't think there have been any upgrades this season, at least among the top teams, that haven't worked," Stella explained. "Even when we introduced some new parts in Baku, after which it appeared that we had taken a step backwards, that wasn't actually the case. Competitiveness has to be assessed in relation to your rivals, not simply by looking at your own progress in absolute terms. And from that perspective, I don't believe we ever took any steps backwards during the season."

The distinction is fundamental. McLaren improved gradually throughout the season, but not enough to compensate for the progress made by its rivals. Above all, it had to recover from an initial deficit that was considerably greater than anyone might have imagined.

"We established that, at the start of the season, we were three months behind in terms of development," said Stella.

This is a significant admission, particularly because the Italian makes clear that this was not an assessment made retrospectively by translating the gap in lap times into months of work. McLaren had already identified the problem by analysing its development trends during 2025.

Stella acknowledges the impact of what happened during the previous championship battle. McLaren had planned to gradually redirect its resources towards the 2026 project, but Red Bull's resurgence in the second half of the championship meant it had to maintain a strong focus on the MCL39 which was still competing on track.

On top of this came an especially complex management challenge: supporting the championship ambitions of both Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri while maintaining an internal balance that would not jeopardise the team's future.

"For me, it was probably the season in which I worked harder than in any of my 26 seasons in F1," said Stella. "Every day, you had to pay attention to managing the team's environment, as well as the technical and operational aspects."

This is one of the less visible aspects of McLaren's story. The team had to devote its energy not only to developing the car and defending its competitiveness, but also to managing a delicate sporting situation. This effort, combined with the technical difficulties, contributed to slowing preparations for 2026.

There is, however, a second element Stella considers decisive. For years, McLaren had demonstrated that a customer team could win a world championship using the same power unit as a works outfit. In 2026, that situation changed.

"In 2025, I was often asked whether not being a works team was a problem," said Stella. "I always said no, and in fact it had never been a problem until the end of last season."

With the introduction of the new power units, the situation became considerably more complicated. Integrating the engine into the car and optimising energy-management parameters took on decisive importance. Mercedes HPP, tasked with developing a competitive and reliable power unit, had to establish its priorities.

"When you're a customer team, you're not the priority," Stella acknowledged. "When it came to understanding the engine's power curves, certain cooling aspects or optimising the integration, we arrived a little late."

One concrete example involved the gearbox ratios, which had been defined using power curves that did not perfectly match those subsequently observed on track. These might appear to be marginal differences, but under the new technical regulations they can translate into significant disadvantages.

"In such a competitive F1 environment, you cannot afford to give away one or two tenths as a structural disadvantage simply because you're not in a position to be at the cutting edge of development timing," he added.

The most sensitive issue, however, concerns the tools used to optimise the power unit's operation. Some software developed jointly by Mercedes HPP and the works team contained proprietary elements that could not be shared with McLaren.

"They told us that these tools contained a significant amount of Mercedes intellectual property and that they couldn't give them to us," Stella said. "I didn't have particularly strong arguments with which to say, 'You have to give them to us anyway'."

The solution was to develop equivalent tools with HPP, essentially repeating some of the work that had already been carried out between Brackley and Brixworth. This process took time, and it is only in 2027 that McLaren will have full access to the same optimisation capabilities.

title: "Disappointed" and "no excuses" – Oliver Bearman frustrated by lack of 2027 F1 contract
article_text:
Following confirmation that Liam Lawson and Valtteri Bottas will remain on the grid, only one seat formally remains vacant for the 2027 Formula 1 season. It is the Haas seat currently occupied by Oliver Bearman.

There is virtually no doubt in the paddock that Bearman will also be on the F1 grid next year, but he finds the delay extremely frustrating, as he made clear in Las Vegas when speaking to media including Motorsport.com.

"There is nothing new to say. If I'm honest, I'm quite disappointed that I'm sitting here at round 20 without a contract signed for next year. It's been a strange situation, but we're getting there," Bearman said.

"All I can say is that it's a bit disappointing and obviously it's not ideal for a driver's confidence and things like that. Of course, I know that I've done a good job this year, but the fact that I don't know what I'm doing next year is not ideal. I'll tell you that much."

Bearman preferred to avoid the question of who exactly he is disappointed with during the media day in Sin City: "I'm not going to comment on that."

It is particularly frustrating for Bearman that he feels good progress has been made in recent weeks, yet it has still not been enough to announce an agreement, while all his fellow drivers on the grid already know where they stand.

"It's very clear that I'm trying to stay at Haas and that I deserve to stay at Haas. At least I feel that way. It's just a strange situation," he said.

"I really thought that we had made decent progress in the last triple header, but maybe it doesn't seem that way. It's a little disappointing. I hope that we can get to the end of this weekend and that I have some good news to tell you."

Bearman completely ruled out racing for any F1 team other than Haas in 2027, something that already appears impossible given that all the other seats have been filled.

Asked by Motorsport.com whether there is a risk that he will ultimately have to settle for a compromise – signing a deal for 2027 but not getting the long-term prospects he wants for the years beyond – he continued: "My goal for 2027 is very clear. I think we have unfinished business here.

"Then looking further into the future, it's not really in my hands, let's say it like that. It's not my avenue. I'm driving the car, but from what I've understood, it's been a challenging one."

The delay appears to be mainly related to his longer-term prospects. In Mexico, Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu dismissed speculation about excessive salary demands as “complete nonsense”, suggesting that the discussions are more likely to revolve around Bearman's future beyond 2027.

The 21-year-old Briton is still affiliated with Ferrari, but acknowledges that it is difficult to get any guarantees about a potential future with the Scuderia.

"I'm under contract with Ferrari. Ferrari have given me this incredible opportunity to step into F1 with them for the first time," he said. "I'm still a Ferrari junior driver and my ultimate dream is to race for Ferrari. They're the most iconic team and they're the first team that believed in me as a kid.

"It's still my ultimate dream, but there's no doubt that looking into the future, there may be some challenges there. There's no denying that, it's very clear. I don't really have much say in the matter. We just need to see how things develop over time."

Regardless of the exact cause and who is to blame, Bearman is particularly uncomfortable with still facing uncertainty with only a few weeks remaining until the winter break.

"Like I said, we are getting there, but it's not a good feeling to be sitting here with two races to go without things sorted out," he said.

"Even though I know that we're pretty much there, the fact is that we're not. There's no excuse for being here without a contract signed, quite honestly."

title: Mansoor bin Mohammed leads UAE delegation at 38th meeting of GCC Olympic Committee Presidents
article_text:
His Highness Sheikh Mansoor bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, President of the UAE Olympic Committee, led the UAE delegation at the 38th meeting of the Presidents of the Olympic Committees of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, held in the Kingdom of Bahrain today.

Upon His Highness’s arrival at Bahrain International Airport, he was received by Sheikh Khalid bin Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, President of the Bahrain Olympic Committee. Ahead of the meeting, His Highness joined the Presidents of the Olympic Committees of GCC countries, for a group photograph.

The UAE delegation included His Excellency Faris Mohammed Al Mutawa, Secretary General of the UAE Olympic Committee; His Excellency Dr. Nasser Al Tamimi, Board Member of the Committee and Vice President of the UAE Judo Federation; and His Excellency Fahad Mohammed Salem bin Kardous Al Ameri, UAE Ambassador to the Kingdom of Bahrain.

The meeting discussed a range of topics aimed at strengthening Gulf sports cooperation, foremost among them supporting Doha’s bid to host the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games, developing the regulatory frameworks governing Gulf sports federations, and enabling the Sports Advisory Committee to fulfil its role at GCC multi-sport Games.

The discussions covered the final versions of the statutes governing Gulf sports federations, the procedures for establishing federations and relocating their headquarters between member states, and the mechanisms by which the Executive Office examines applications to establish federations and submits them to the Council of Olympic Committee Presidents. It also covered the continuous monitoring and evaluation of federation performance.

The meeting also examined the responsibilities of the Sports Advisory Committee at GCC multi-sport Games, alongside a proposal to establish a four-member subcommittee comprising representatives of the country holding the current presidency, the host country, the country due to assume the next presidency, and the General Secretariat. The proposed subcommittee would monitor preparations and the fulfilment of commitments by national Olympic committees, participate in coordination and technical meetings and meetings of chefs de mission, and follow competitions during the Games.

The discussions addressed the UAE’s initiative to host the fourth GCC Beach Games in 2027, following Bahrain’s withdrawal from hosting the event due to its commitment to hosting the Arab Games in the same year and the associated organisational, technical and logistical obligations. Discussions also covered follow-up on the completion of the necessary procedures and official approvals with the relevant authorities in the UAE.

In the same context, the meeting reviewed a proposal by the UAE Olympic Committee to hold a Sports Law and Management Conference on the sidelines of the 2027 GCC Beach Games, should they be held in the UAE.

The meeting reviewed the final report on the fourth GCC Games – Doha 2026, covering its data and information, technical and organisational aspects, challenges and recommendations. It also discussed referring the report to the Executive Office and the relevant committees for review and necessary action, while expressing appreciation for Qatar’s efforts in making the Games a success.

The meeting further discussed the schedule of GCC multi-sport Games for 2029–2032 and aligning their dates with regional and international sporting commitments. Discussions took into account Saudi Arabia’s earlier withdrawal from hosting the 2024 Gulf Indoor and Martial Arts Games, the UAE’s initiative to host the 2027 GCC Beach Games, Kuwait’s hosting of the second GCC Youth Games in 2028, and Qatar’s withdrawal from hosting the Games scheduled for 2029–2031 due to its commitments to major sporting events. The meeting also explored the possibility of Bahrain, Saudi Arabia and the Sultanate of Oman hosting the remaining Games, depending on their respective circumstances and capabilities.

Other matters included following up on the implementation of decisions taken at the 37th meeting of the Council of GCC Olympic Committee Presidents and coordinating with Saudi Arabia, which will assume the presidency for the next term, to determine the date and venue of the Council’s 39th meeting, to be preceded by a preparatory meeting of the Executive Office.

title: Wellstar Health named as naming rights partner for Atlanta City FC women’s soccer facility
article_text:
The recently minted Atlanta City FC pro women's soccer team in metro Atlanta is ramping up operations and it now has a partner for its training facility.

Wellstar Health System was announced as the Atlanta City FC's naming rights partner for the team's training facility, making the facility the Wellstar Performance Center, according to officials.

The AMB Sports and Entertainment company said Wellstar was named on the facility as part of a joint commitment to supporting female athletes.

As part of the agreement, Wellstar will work with AMBSE for several years to construct a world-class facility specifically for female athletes.

"From the outset, we committed to constructing a state-of-the-art performance center for Atlanta City FC and equipping our club with the necessary resources to compete for championships," said President of Soccer, AMBSE Mauricio Culebro. "We are excited to have Wellstar help bring this vision to life and lend their expertise to ensure our athletes receive best-in-class care to help them perform at their best. We are also confident Wellstar Performance Center will serve as a key recruiting tool as we look to welcome world-class players to Atlanta City FC ahead of our NWSL debut in 2028."

In addition to building the facility together through the partnership with Atlanta City FC and AMBSE, Wellstar Health System will also serve as the team's official healthcare provider.

Wellstar will also be the training apparel partner for the club team, according to the announcement. This includes matchday activations and fan engagement at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, digital signage and match sponsorship.

The two companies will also create a joint philanthropic program to host women's health events and orthopedics at the Wellstar Performance Center, once construction is complete.

"Atlanta City FC and Wellstar share a commitment to helping people thrive, both on and off the field," said Ketul J. Patel, President and CEO of Wellstar Health System." Through this partnership, we'll support the club's athletes while creating new ways to connect with women, families, and communities across the region. We are honored to be selected as the club's healthcare partner and to work alongside an organization that reflects Arthur Blank's long-standing commitment to improving lives across Georgia."

Patel said the team-up is "a reflection of the exceptional care our physicians and team members provide every day," adding that the health system was looking forward to the fruits of the partnership.

AMBSE owner Arthur Blank said he was thrilled to welcome Wellstar Health System as the official healthcare provider for Atlanta City FC.

"Our family of businesses and Wellstar share a foundational belief about the importance of making a difference in the community, and we are proud to represent a Georgia-based organization at the home of our new club," Blank said in a statement. "I'd like to thank Ketul Patel and the entire team at Wellstar for their unwavering commitment to supporting our athletes, as well as our executive leadership team for bringing this partnership to life."

title: RCB signs shirt sponsorship deal with Qatar Airways
article_text:
Qatar Airways announce their latest partnership with club cricket giants – the Royal Challengers Bangalore (RCB), becoming the Indian Premier League (IPL) team’s Official Front of Jersey Partner.

The Indian Premier 2023 season will take place between 31 March – 28 May, with the Bengaluru based cricket team playing their opening match on 2 April against the Mumbai Indians. In the presence of 40,000 fans, RCB’s home arena – the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium, hosted a special “Unboxing Event” that featured cricket legends, celebrities, team officials and the likes of cricket superstars Virat Kohli, Faf du Plessis and Glen Maxwell. Fans watched the RCB squad train in an entertaining atmosphere, after which the Qatar Airways cabin crew greeted the team during a special jersey unveiling ceremony.

The airline’s leisure division – Qatar Airways Holidays, is exclusively launching all-inclusive travel packages, allowing cricket fans to attend an IPL match at the bespoke Qatar Airways hospitality lounge at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium. In addition, the packages will enable fans to partake in exclusive experiences such as viewing practice sessions, signed memorabilia, player meet and greet, photo opportunity with Virat Kholi, and more. The Ultimate RCB Fan packages include return flights with Qatar Airways, premium hotel options, IPL tickets and exciting experiences. To secure packages, customers can visit the dedicated link, qatarairways.com/RCB.

Qatar Airways group chief executive, Akbar Al Baker, said: “We embark on a new journey with the addition of the Royal Challengers Bangalore to our extensive sports portfolio. The team has a passionate fanbase and a well-represented list of cricket legends that have played for the team. Cricket is a global game with a world-wide audience and is a powerful means of uniting people of different backgrounds. From start to end, our RCB packages will take the fan experience to the next level with a seamless journey to witness world-class cricket and entertainment.”

“Qatar Airways regards India as an important market where we operate non-stop flights from 13 Indian cities. Our operations from India also serve connections to 13 cities in North America and 35 cities in Europe through our hub – Hamad International Airport, which was awarded Skytrax World’s Best Airport award for the past two years. We are excited to partner with RCB over the next three years in what we trust will be a successful alliance.”

Chairman of Royal Challengers Bangalore and chief commercial officer of Diageo India, Prathmesh Mishra, said: “We are thrilled at the potential of the RCB – Qatar Airways partnership. The synergies between both brands serve as a robust platform to build a very strong marketing association over the next three years and beyond. Qatar Airways has a strong demonstrative history of activating world class sports marketing partnerships and we hope the RCB partnership is just as successful. The partnership and its activation will be a benchmark in the Indian sports ecosystem and adds to the aspiration of RCB on its pathway to becoming a global cricketing powerhouse and a lifestyle brand.”

The “Unboxing Event” paved the way for several entertainment activities, featuring musical performances from various acts, including international artist – Jason Derulo, who performed live at the stadium. In addition, cricket legends A.B. de Villiers and Chris Gayle’s jerseys were officially retired by the team as a mark of honour to induct them into the club’s hall of fame.

Qatar Airways has recently launched a new brand campaign in collaboration with world-renowned Indian actor, Deepika Padukone, who encapsulates the premium experience available to customers of Qatar Airways, transiting through the best airport in the Middle East – Hamad International Airport.

Qatar Airways as a brand is committed to supporting global sports, helping fans travel to their favourite events wherever they may be. The airline is a leading global football supporter, with partnerships including FIFA, Paris Saint-Germain, FC Bayern and Concacaf. Additionally, Qatar Airways is the Official Airline of Formula 1®, the Ironman and Ironman 70.3 Triathlon Series, United Rugby Championship (URC), Global Kitesports Association and multiple other disciplines including equestrianism, padel, squash and tennis.Hit for a Six: Qatar Airways Welcomes Cricket Giants – Royal Challengers Bangalore to its Diverse Sports Sponsorship Portfolio.

title: Fenway Sports Group needs Brad Keselowski’s approval to buy into Cadillac F1
article_text:
Fenway Sports Group’s reported pursuit of an ownership stake in the Cadillac Formula 1 Team could be stalled by an unexpected roadblock: a NASCAR driver.

FSG, which also owns Liverpool and the Boston Red Sox, is among several parties in talks to buy billionaire Mark Walter’s stake in the Cadillac F1 team. But two racing industry sources familiar with the agreement told The Athletic that driver Brad Keselowski and FSG’s contract stipulates that neither can pursue a motorsports venture outside NASCAR without the other’s permission.

title: Christian Horner Drops Major Hint on Alpine Formula 1 Team Stake
article_text:
Christian Horner has dropped a major hint about a potential return to F1, suggesting that he would only consider investing his efforts in a team if he had the authority to influence meaningful change. Horner has been linked with a possible investment in Alpine, with minority shareholder Otro Capital reportedly exploring a sale of its 24% stake in the team.

During an interview with Vincenzo Landino, the former Red Bull boss shed light on the possibility of purchasing the minority stake in Alpine.

"What is the point in buying a minority stake if you can't influence change? There's no point investing in a team that you can't drive change into. So for me that would be nonsensical to do something like that," Horner said [5:10]

Horner was sacked from his role as CEO and Team Principal of Red Bull Racing on July 9, 2025. His sudden exit marked the end of his 20-year tenure with the Milton Keynes-based team.

Despite being linked with several potential opportunities, Horner, who had secured multiple drivers' and constructors' championships for Red Bull, has indicated that he is in no rush to return to the F1 paddock.

"I'd only want to go back if, you know, first of all I had equity in a project and secondly that I was in a position to enable change. I won pretty much a third of the races that I ever competed in," Horner said.

The Briton also pointed to his achievements at Red Bull as evidence of what he could accomplish with the right resources and commitment.

"I don't want to go back just to take part. I'm not afraid of taking on a project, and certainly you know my time at Red Bull demonstrated that if you have a desire and a commitment you can achieve anything – whether it's with a chassis or even obviously laterally with the engine," he added.

The former Red Bull team principal also acknowledged how dramatically Formula 1 team valuations have increased alongside the sport's commercial growth, particularly in the United States.

"Well, valuations of the teams are just going off the charts at the moment because of the success of Formula 1. You look at how the sport has grown, particularly in the US over the last few years. The franchises now have real value to them," Horner said.

"I mean, six/seven/eight years ago, half of the grid would have been pretty much insolvent. Now the smallest team in Formula 1 has at least a $2 billion valuation."

Otro Capital acquired a 24% minority stake in Alpine in 2023 and has reportedly appointed investment bank BDT & MSD Partners to explore a potential sale.

According to GPFans, the stake is now estimated to be worth approximately $787 million, based on a reported total team valuation of $3.28 billion (a 58 percent increase on 2025).
