Big Sky Dips Toe Into Women’s Swimming Sponsorship with Five Members
article_text:
The Big Sky Conference will sponsor women’s swimming and diving in 2027-28, starting with a five-team field.

Member institutions Idaho, Northern Arizona, Northern Colorado and Utah Tech will join the league’s launch. University of Texas Rio Grande Valley will join for the first time as an affiliate member.

All five schools jump from the Mountain Pacific Sports Federation, whose expansion in women’s swimming to 24 teams appears to be a one-year gambit.

“We are absolutely thrilled to introduce women’s swimming and diving as the newest Big Sky-sponsored sport,” Big Sky Conference Commissioner Tom Wistrcill said in a press release last week. “In this era of college athletics, it’s particularly meaningful that our membership has leaned into crowning another team each year as a Big Sky champion and, in doing so, will create a direct pathway for additional Big Sky student-athletes to qualify for and participate in their respective NCAA championship. I applaud the administrations at our four current full members that sponsor this sport for embracing this opportunity, and on behalf of our entire membership also eagerly welcome the UTRGV Vaqueros to our conference as an affiliate.”

The Big Sky sponsored men’s swimming and diving from 1963-74. This is the first time that it will sponsor women’s swimming and diving. It is the 10th women’s sport and 17th total sport in the Big Sky’s championship portfolio.

“I’m very excited to see women’s swimming and diving join the Big Sky Conference,” Big Sky SAAC Executive Board member and Idaho diver Amelia Ward said. “As a student-athlete at the University of Idaho, I look forward to competing against universities that already share a competitive relationship with other athletic teams at our school. I believe this will foster camaraderie among student-athletes and strengthen our university’s athletic community.”

title: ‘No excuse’: Ollie Bearman frustrated by lack of Haas F1 contract with 3 races left
Lewis Hamilton identifies 'main focus' ahead of Las Vegas Grand Prix as Ferrari eye 'big changes' for 2027
article_text:
Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc are targeting a strong end to 2026 as Ferrari fight for P2 and look ahead to next season.

Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc have stressed the importance of finishing the 2026 season strongly as Ferrari look to bounce back from a challenging Sao Paulo Grand Prix, with the team focused on securing P2 in the Constructors' Championship and gathering valuable information ahead of next year.

Ferrari arrive in Las Vegas after Leclerc and Hamilton finished eighth and ninth respectively in Brazil, but Hamilton remains determined to deliver a result that would mean a great deal to those working behind the scenes at Maranello.

"The Constructors' Championship is the main focus," Hamilton said during media day in Las Vegas. "The main focus is making sure we solidify second in the Constructors' for the team, because that's something that means a huge amount to everyone back at the factory, but especially to me also.

"That's what we're working towards and then, if we're able to do well and keep in the battle for these last few races, maybe we can climb back up from fourth and hopefully be in the top three."

Looking ahead to 2027, Hamilton explained that the remaining three races would also offer opportunities to experiment with different setups and gather data, despite Ferrari having no new components available to test.

"This is a really important period of time," he explained. "We don't have any new components to test, but this is definitely a really important data point for us to understand and make some changes setup-wise, and try some things that we can potentially use to see if everything's working.

"There's some big changes for next year. But otherwise, right now we also have the focus on trying to make sure we maintain second in the Constructors' Championship. That's the focus."

Leclerc echoed his team mate's desire to finish the campaign positively, explaining that maintaining momentum heading into the winter break would be important for morale within Ferrari, while admitting that he is more concerned with securing further victories than his final Drivers' Championship position.

"My main focus at the moment is to try and win races, and the natural result of winning races will hopefully be second place in the Drivers' Championship," he said.

"I just want to finish the season on a high, for sure, in order to keep that good momentum. It's always important to finish the season on a high, particularly because the winter break is quite long, and for the motivation of everyone, it would be nice."

However, the Monegasque driver acknowledged that Ferrari could face another challenging weekend in Las Vegas, with cold temperatures and the circuit's long straights presenting particular concerns following the team's struggles with tyre warm-up in Brazil.

"We don't have any quick fixes, otherwise we would have put them on the car a long time ago," Leclerc admitted.

"There are things we cannot change now, and there are things that we can control and put our focus on. And that is the tyre warm-up, for example, that will be quite critical.

"If we do a very good job on that, I think it can outweigh maybe the disadvantage that we have power unit-wise. I remain hopeful, but it's going to be a big challenge for us."

title: John Terry and Kevin Durant back MWS growth
article_text:
MWS has secured £15.5m in new investment from a group of sports investors led by Gamma Waves Partners & John Terry to support its international expansion

The investment in MWS, previously known as MatchWornShirt, includes backing from former England and Chelsea captain John Terry and NBA player Kevin Durant through 35V, his investment company with Rich Kleiman.

Gamma Waves Partners is the lead investor in the round. The sports and technology investment platform was Co-Founded by former Italy international Giorgio Chiellini, former Juventus chairman Andrea Agnelli and Rocco Benetton.

Other investors include Pacers Sports & Entertainment, the ownership group behind the Indiana Pacers and Indiana Fever, and Joyned Capital, whose members include Arsenal player Jurriën Timber and his brother Quinten Timber. Tottenham Hotspur defender Tosin Adarabioyo has also invested individually.

The funding will support the sports memorabilia platform’s expansion, including further growth in North America. MWS has established partnerships across football and has expanded into sports including basketball, ice hockey, rugby and cycling.

Founded in Amsterdam in 2017 by brothers Tijmen Zonderwijk and Bob Zonderwijk, MWS operates an online auction platform for authenticated match-worn sports memorabilia. Its partnership portfolio includes more than 450 clubs globally, with Chelsea among its UK football partners.

Tijmen Zonderwijk, Co-Founder and CEO of MWS, said, “The scale of the names and businesses involved in this group of investors demonstrates a collective passion for what we have already built here at MWS, and for that, we’re incredibly proud. It also represents a shared vision for the future, and we’re excited to accelerate the growth of the business whilst remaining true to our values.

“All involved across this group of investors have core experience in the world of sport and entertainment, but more widely than that, building businesses that sit at the intersection of sport, culture, commerce and community. This is where it becomes an even more exciting prospect; building on a shared vision to bring fans and collectors around the world closer to the moments and the icons that are central to their sporting passions.”

title: Fernando Alonso rules out staying in F1 for V8 return: "16 years of pure racing lost"
article_text:
Although the FIA's formal confirmation on Tuesday was only online for a few minutes before being temporarily taken down again, it is clear to everyone in the paddock that V8 engines will return to Formula 1.

The agreement in principle involves a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 – with the turbo being particularly important for Audi and Honda – and a significantly smaller electrical component. The target for its introduction is 2030, which would be a year earlier than initially planned.

It is largely what the drivers have been pushing for, which explains the positive reactions in the Las Vegas paddock during the media day.

Fernando Alonso, however, stressed to media including Motorsport.com that the V8 return will come too late for him. The Spaniard is currently 45 and, perhaps unsurprisingly, has no intention of remaining in the pinnacle of motorsport for another four years: "No, I will not be around for the new V8. 100%."

When it was pointed out that Alonso has surprised people in the paddock before, for example with his F1 comeback in 2021, he laughed: "Yeah, I have surprised myself in the past as well! But this time I think it's the good one. When I stop, it will be the moment, also the moment to try different things.

"It's still a long way ahead, [the V8 return], but I think it will be enough [for me before that]."

Alonso does find it frustrating, in a sense, that he will have to bow out under a set of regulations that he, like many other drivers, is far from fond of: "Yes, it's frustrating that we didn't have it in 2014 already. From 2014 to 2030 or 2031, so that means 16 years or 17 years of pure racing are lost."

While Alonso will no longer be competing in F1 by then, he still has his sights set on other racing categories. Even after retiring from F1, Alonso intends to continue racing for a long time.

In January 2027, he will make an appearance at the Dakar Rally, but he is also leaving the door open to other iconic races once his F1 career comes to an end.

"Dakar was on my mind. Le Mans is on my mind, the Indy 500 is on my mind," the Aston Martin driver said.

"I love competing and I love competing in race cars in which you have power when you go on throttle, and in which you have deceleration when you brake. Those are the things that we miss now in Formula 1.

"Obviously, if I continue in Formula 1, that will always be my priority and it's difficult to put things together or to combine different programs. Dakar, because it's in January, it fits a little bit better, but even that had to come with a few coincidences."

That Alonso would like to return to endurance races such as Le Mans is no surprise – he would even like to do so alongside Max Verstappen – but his mention of the Indy 500 is somewhat more unexpected.

After his last attempt in 2020, the Spaniard did not seem particularly keen on another appearance at The Greatest Spectacle in Racing at the Brickyard, but with a new IndyCar chassis on the way, his opinion could change.

"Yeah, I don't know. They will change cars soon. There's a new car coming for 2028, I think, so yeah, I don't know," he said. "I may consider it one day. It’s not in my short-term plans and not on my mind now, but I cannot say no to it 100%."

title: Bank of America Youth Sports Platform Sports with Us Launches in Italy With PlayMore!
article_text:
- Bank of America named PlayMore! as the delivery partner for its Sports with Us youth sports platform in Italy, announced November 16 in Milan.

- Sports with Us now spans 15 countries and provides access to sports for more than 1.2 million children, according to the bank.

- The Italy launch expands the PlayMore! United program, pairing weekly training sessions with lessons in leadership, nutrition and financial education.

- Outside the U.S., the bank aims to positively impact more than 10,000 young people across 14 countries by the end of 2028.

Bank of America has named PlayMore!, an established sport-for-development organization, as the delivery partner for Sports with Us in Italy. The launch extends the Bank of America youth sports platform, which the bank says now spans 15 countries and provides access to sports for more than 1.2 million children, according to its November 16, 2026 announcement from Milan.

Sports with Us combines sport, mentoring and education with the stated goal of helping young people build confidence, develop life skills and access pathways to education, per the release.

The Italian rollout will support the expansion of the PlayMore! United program, which pairs regular sport participation with structured life-skills development. Participants will attend weekly “United” training sessions alongside practical learning in leadership, teamwork, communication, wellbeing, nutrition and financial education, the bank said.

According to the release, the curriculum modules were built specifically for Sports with Us in collaboration with global universities and educational institutions, which were not named. The bank’s FAQ adds that sport-based activities are led by Athlete Mentors.

Vito Luca Lo Piccolo, Country Executive for Bank of America Italy, framed the program around access: “Sport has the power to open doors.” He said the partnership with PlayMore! is meant to create pathways for young people to build brighter futures.

Who Is PlayMore!, the Italy Delivery Partner?

PlayMore! has worked on an inclusion principle since 2010, according to President Luigi De Micco, who said the organization believes “sport brings people together on equal terms, regardless of their starting point.” De Micco said Sports with Us lets PlayMore! extend that approach to more young people in Milan and across Italy, with added focus on confidence, wellbeing and independence.

Najla Aqdeir, a coach and ambassador for PlayMore!, said she sees daily how teamwork, discipline, leadership and resilience learned through sport carry into other parts of young people’s lives.

Bank of America describes Sports with Us as part of its commitment to leave a lasting legacy after serving as the Official Bank of the FIFA World Cup 2026. Outside the United States, the bank says the platform supports an ambition to positively impact more than 10,000 young people across 14 countries by the end of 2028.

Italy follows the United Kingdom, where Bank of America named the Youth Sport Trust as its Sports with Us delivery partner, building on an existing relationship. The Youth Sport Trust, founded in 1995, works with around 20,000 schools and provides opportunities for more than two million children each year, according to the organization.

The structure in both markets is the same: the bank’s platform is delivered by an established local organization with its own existing programming. In Italy, that means weekly United sessions in Milan with a stated path to other parts of the country.

The release does not disclose the size of Bank of America’s financial commitment, how many participants PlayMore! United will reach, or which Italian cities follow Milan, the figures that will show how much of the 10,000-person target Italy is expected to carry.

title: Saudi Arabia begins enforcing 15% Saudization requirement across 12 sports professions
article_text:
RIYADH — The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) announced that a decision requiring 15 percent Saudization of designated professions in private-sector sports centers and gyms took effect on Wednesday, November 18, 2026.

The measure, implemented in partnership with the Ministry of Sport following the end of the grace period granted to affected establishments, aims to create quality employment opportunities for Saudi men and women and increase the participation of national talent in specialized sports professions.

The ministry explained that private-sector establishments employing four or more workers in the targeted professions are now required to Saudize 15 percent of positions in those professions.

The decision covers 12 professions in men's and women's sports centers and gyms, including sports coaches, fitness trainers, professional football coaches, professional racket sports coaches, professional water sports coaches, personal sports trainers, professional athletics coaches, sports supervisors, professional ice sports coaches, professional equestrian coaches, professional self-defense sports coaches and professional ball sports coaches.

MHRSD inspection teams have begun conducting inspections across the Kingdom to verify establishments' compliance with the required Saudization percentage and take legally prescribed measures, including penalties, against violators.

The ministry urged private-sector establishments covered by the decision to comply with the Saudization requirement and review the procedural guidelines published on its official website.

It also emphasized the importance of reporting violations of Saudization decisions through the ministry's application or by calling its unified number, 19911.

The decision forms part of MHRSD's efforts, in cooperation with the Ministry of Sport, to expand employment opportunities for Saudi men and women and develop specialized national talent to support the future of the Kingdom's sports sector.

title: McLaren to sell 2027 F1 car before it races
article_text:
McLaren will auction its 2027 MCL41 Formula 1 car with Sotheby’s after the 2026 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

A chassis either used by Lando Norris or Oscar Piastri will be offered complete with a 2027-spec Mercedes power unit in the December 9 auction.

The winning bidder will gain “exclusive access” to McLaren with a tour of its Woking headquarters ahead of the 2027 F1 season, plus the opportunity to meet team principal Zak Brown and drivers Norris and Piastri.

The winning bidder will also be invited to McLaren’s 2027 season launch event, the historic triple crown of the Monaco Grand Prix, the Le Mans 24 Hours, and the Indianapolis 500, plus they will also be given hospitality access at two grands prix.

At the end of the 2025 F1 season, McLaren auctioned the 2026 MCL40A F1 car for $11,480,000 USD, making it the first F1 car to be auctioned before being raced.

The winning bidder of the 2026 F1 car will receive it in 2028 “given the strict regulations conceived to prevent rivals from gaining access to relevant intellectual property”. In the meantime, they were offered a 2025 show car for display purposes.

The winning bidder of the 2027 F1 car might expect a similar delay.

The 2027 McLaren F1 car “may be used in designated demonstration runs and at track days” with a team of McLaren engineers and mechanics accompanying the driver to said events.

McLaren auctioned off its 2027 World Endurance Championship Hypercar for $7,598,750 at last year’s Abu Dhabi auction.

This year’s Abu Dhabi auction includes the Adrian Newey-designed Aston Martin Valkyrie ($2.8m-$3.2m) and a Gordon Murray Automotive T.50 ($5.5m-$6m).
